new.description: A BIGINT source can pass destination preflight and finish as succeeded with exact verification while an existing REAL or DOUBLE PRECISION destination silently changes its values. This occurs with the default append policy and no user-selected cast.

1. Create a source table with a BIGINT value of `1000000001` and an existing target with a REAL column.

new.body:
## Description

A BIGINT source can pass destination preflight and finish as succeeded with exact verification while an existing REAL or DOUBLE PRECISION destination silently changes its values. This occurs with the default append policy and no user-selected cast.

Verified October 27, 2026 on commit `2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0`. Baseline: **990 passed**. Audit: **14 passing characterization cases across 8 distinct defects** (including three existing-report matches). Python 3.12.13, Polars 1.44.2, psycopg 3.3.5. No production data or live provider credentials were used.

## Labels

`bug`, `priority: high`.

## Affected Components

- [_validate_destination_column_casts](https://github.com/eddiethedean/user-token-management-app/blob/2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0/app/connectors/postgres.py#L1529)
- [PostgresConnector.prepare_destination](https://github.com/eddiethedean/user-token-management-app/blob/2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0/app/connectors/postgres.py#L716)
- [PostgresConnector.write_batch](https://github.com/eddiethedean/user-token-management-app/blob/2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0/app/connectors/postgres.py#L959)
- [_reconcile_write_result](https://github.com/eddiethedean/user-token-management-app/blob/2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0/app/services/transfer_engine.py#L115)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a source table with a BIGINT value of `1000000001` and an existing target with a REAL column.
2. Select an append route without column-type overrides; run read-only preflight and execute it.
3. Read the destination value and persisted run verification.
4. Repeat with BIGINT `9007199254740993` and a DOUBLE PRECISION target.

Save the following self-contained test outside `tests/`, for example `/tmp/test_bug.py`. Install the repository's development dependencies, then run from the repository root:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest /tmp/test_bug.py -c pyproject.toml -s --tb=short
```

PostgreSQL cases require the local server binaries used by the repository fixtures. All databases and HTTP services are disposable loopback fixtures. Databricks cases use the existing SQL/management harness. **These are characterization assertions: passing means the defect was reproduced.** Invert them when adding regression tests.

<details>
<summary>Executable reproduction</summary>

```python
from __future__ import annotations
import json
from decimal import Decimal
import pytest
from app.config import get_settings
from app.connectors.locators import DefinitionSnapshot, PostgresAppendPolicy, postgres_table
from app.connectors.postgres import PostgresConnector, connect
from app.database import SessionLocal
from app.models import PipelineRun
from app.services.pipeline_runs import claim_run
from app.services.transfer_engine import execute_transfer
from tests.postgres_support import connector_settings

pytest_plugins = ["tests.conftest"]


def _execute_postgres(db, owner, credentials, *, settings=None):
    snapshot = DefinitionSnapshot(
        name="PostgreSQL type audit",
        source_provider="postgres",
        destination_provider="postgres",
        source=postgres_table("public", "audit_source"),
        destination=postgres_table("public", "audit_target"),
        write_policy=PostgresAppendPolicy(),
    )
    run = PipelineRun(user_id=owner.id, definition_snapshot_json=snapshot.model_dump_json())
    db.add(run)
    db.commit()
    run, lease = claim_run(db, worker_id="audit", lease_seconds=120, run_id=run.id)
    execute_transfer(
        db,
        run=run,
        lease_token=lease,
        snapshot=snapshot,
        source_credentials=credentials,
        destination_credentials=credentials,
        settings=settings or get_settings(),
        cancel_requested=lambda: False,
        source_resolver=lambda _: PostgresConnector(connector_settings()),
        destination_resolver=lambda _: PostgresConnector(connector_settings()),
        route_policy=lambda *_: True,
        writer_policy=lambda _: True,
    )
    return run


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("destination_type", "source_value"),
    [("real", 1_000_000_001), ("double precision", 9_007_199_254_740_993)],
)
def test_existing_float_target_silently_rounds_integer(
    access_app, make_user, postgres_credentials, destination_type, source_value
):
    owner = make_user("numeric.audit@example.gov")
    cfg = connector_settings()
    with connect(postgres_credentials, cfg) as conn:
        conn.execute("CREATE TABLE audit_source (value bigint)")
        conn.execute(f"CREATE TABLE audit_target (value {destination_type})")
        conn.execute("INSERT INTO audit_source VALUES (%s)", (source_value,))
    connector = PostgresConnector(cfg)
    source_schema = connector.inspect_object(
        postgres_credentials, postgres_table("public", "audit_source")
    )
    connector.preflight_destination(
        postgres_credentials,
        postgres_table("public", "audit_target"),
        source_schema,
        PostgresAppendPolicy(),
    )
    with SessionLocal() as db:
        run = _execute_postgres(db, owner, postgres_credentials)
        assert run.status == "succeeded"
        assert json.loads(run.verification_json)["verification_level"] == "exact"
    with connect(postgres_credentials, cfg) as conn:
        actual = Decimal.from_float(conn.execute("SELECT value FROM audit_target").fetchone()[0])
    assert actual != Decimal(source_value)
    print(f"Integer {source_value} -> {destination_type} {actual}; run succeeded/exact")
```

</details>

## Expected Behavior

Reject an implicitly lossy numeric route before publication, or require a deliberate, clearly communicated conversion policy. An exact integer must not silently change under the default transfer.

## Actual Behavior

Preflight accepts both routes. REAL stores `1000000000`; DOUBLE PRECISION stores `9007199254740992`. Both runs report `succeeded` and `verification_level: exact`. Values were retrieved as Python floats and converted with Decimal.from_float, avoiding any additional PostgreSQL float-to-NUMERIC display rounding.

## Root Cause Analysis

Compatibility validation asks EXPLAIN whether PostgreSQL permits the assignment; it does not check whether the destination can represent the source numeric domain or actual values exactly. Staging clones the destination float type, so COPY has already rounded the integer before finalization. Decimal-specific safeguards do not cover integer sources. Row-count reconciliation cannot detect changed values.

## Impact

Identifiers, counters, and exact integer measures can be corrupted in an otherwise successful production transfer. All row-count checks can pass, leaving the problem invisible in the monitor. The reproduced path uses real disposable PostgreSQL databases and the real transfer engine.

## Suggested Fix

Extend destination compatibility checks to integer-to-floating-point and other narrowing numeric conversions. Reject values outside the target exact-integer range unless an explicit conversion is chosen; preserve an exact staging representation until that decision is enforced. Keep row-count verification accurately distinguished from value-fidelity guarantees.

## Test Coverage Gaps

The baseline checks decimal preservation and row-count reconciliation, but misses BIGINT-to-existing-REAL/DOUBLE routes. Add append/upsert/replace coverage at and just outside the exact-integer boundaries, asserting stored values and run outcomes, with and without explicit overrides.

## Severity

High

## Confidence

High — reproduced locally through the code paths and boundaries identified above.

## Existing Issue Matches

Reviewed all open issues (0 at audit start), 100 recently updated closed issues, the prior audit, and the complete patches of open documentation PRs #151 and #153. Each finding also received function/error/symptom searches across all issue states and open PRs. README, provider notes, the worker runbook, and relevant security decisions were checked for expected limitations.

Searched `_validate_destination_column_casts`, PostgreSQL/integer/precision/rounding/float, and related symptoms across all issue states. #11 concerns a Decimal source mapped to floating point when creating a new table; #78 concerns CSV parsing; #74 concerns Foundry batch promotion. This report uses native integer sources and an already existing PostgreSQL target. #27 is the separate temporal-semantics variant. No matching open fix was found.

new.title: [BUG] Run retention deletes unresolved Databricks publication records and target fences
new.description: The retention janitor deletes Databricks publication evidence while recovery is unresolved. It purges succeeded runs with pending staging cleanup, and reviewed uncertain runs whose publication still owns an active target fence. Deleting the run cascades to the publication row.
new.steps:
1. Persist a terminal run older than PIPELINE_RUN_RETENTION_DAYS and an associated DatabricksPublication.
2. For the first case use state `uncertain`, an active_target_key, and a failed_needs_reconciliation run; record an operator reconciliation review.
3. For the second case use state `cleanup_pending`, a confirmed commit, and a succeeded run.
4. Run the real retention janitor, then query both the run and publication tables.
new.expected: Retain unresolved publication evidence and any active target fence until provider reconciliation and required cleanup finish, regardless of the ordinary run-retention cutoff or a recorded operator review.
new.actual: Both runs are purged and their publication rows disappear through ON DELETE CASCADE. The uncertain case loses its active target fence; the confirmed-commit case loses the only durable record directing staging cleanup. Both cases pass executable characterization assertions.
new.cause: janitor checks only run-level reconciliation requirements/review flags before deletion. It never checks DatabricksPublication.state, active_target_key, or pending cleanup. The foreign key cascades deletion to the durable operation table, bypassing its recovery lifecycle and uniqueness fence.
new.impact: A long-unresolved publication can lose its recovery/audit evidence and the database constraint that prevents another publication to the same target. Confirmed publications can leave remote staging data indefinitely. Defaults allow this after 90 days; supported shorter retention settings shorten the window. Loss of the fence is verified in persistence; no live duplicate Databricks write was attempted.
new.fix: Protect runs and their events whenever an associated publication is unresolved, owns a fence, or still needs staging cleanup. Resolve the provider operation before allowing run deletion, or retain publication evidence independently with suitable referential integrity. Operator review must not substitute for provider commit/cleanup confirmation.
new.gaps: The existing janitor test protects an unreviewed uncertain run but does not attach a DatabricksPublication. Recovery tests cover operation states independently of run retention. Add both reproduced cases, an unreviewed control, and resolved complete/unchanged publication controls.
new.dedup: Searched janitor, retention, DatabricksPublication, cascade, fence, and cleanup. #158 concerns a committed record excluded from the recovery selector; that selector now includes committed, but this report concerns deletion of the record itself by a different service. No existing report or open PR covers the retention/cascade defect.
new.body:
## Description

The retention janitor deletes Databricks publication evidence while recovery is unresolved. It purges succeeded runs with pending staging cleanup, and reviewed uncertain runs whose publication still owns an active target fence. Deleting the run cascades to the publication row.

Verified October 27, 2026 on commit `2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0`. Baseline: **990 passed**. Audit: **14 passing characterization cases across 8 distinct defects** (including three existing-report matches). Python 3.12.13, Polars 1.44.2, psycopg 3.3.5. No production data or live provider credentials were used.

## Labels

`bug`, `priority: high`.

## Affected Components

- [janitor](https://github.com/eddiethedean/user-token-management-app/blob/2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0/app/services/pipeline_runs.py#L1272)
- [DatabricksPublication foreign key and unique target fence](https://github.com/eddiethedean/user-token-management-app/blob/2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0/app/models.py#L311)
- [record_reconciliation_review](https://github.com/eddiethedean/user-token-management-app/blob/2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0/app/services/pipeline_runs.py#L386)
- [process_pending_publication_recovery](https://github.com/eddiethedean/user-token-management-app/blob/2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0/app/services/databricks_publication.py#L180)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Persist a terminal run older than PIPELINE_RUN_RETENTION_DAYS and an associated DatabricksPublication.
2. For the first case use state `uncertain`, an active_target_key, and a failed_needs_reconciliation run; record an operator reconciliation review.
3. For the second case use state `cleanup_pending`, a confirmed commit, and a succeeded run.
4. Run the real retention janitor, then query both the run and publication tables.

Save the following self-contained test outside `tests/`, for example `/tmp/test_bug.py`. Install the repository's development dependencies, then run from the repository root:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest /tmp/test_bug.py -c pyproject.toml -s --tb=short
```

PostgreSQL cases require the local server binaries used by the repository fixtures. All databases and HTTP services are disposable loopback fixtures. Databricks cases use the existing SQL/management harness. **These are characterization assertions: passing means the defect was reproduced.** Invert them when adding regression tests.

<details>
<summary>Executable reproduction</summary>

```python
from __future__ import annotations
from datetime import timedelta
import pytest
from app.config import get_settings
from app.database import SessionLocal
from app.models import DatabricksPublication, PipelineRun, utcnow
from app.services.pipeline_runs import janitor, record_reconciliation_review
from tests.test_databricks_connector import _table_locator

pytest_plugins = ["tests.conftest"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("publication_state", ["uncertain", "cleanup_pending"])
def test_retention_deletes_pending_publication(access_app, make_user, publication_state):
    owner = make_user("retention.audit@example.gov")
    stale = utcnow() - timedelta(days=100)
    settings = get_settings()
    with SessionLocal() as db:
        run = PipelineRun(
            user_id=owner.id,
            definition_snapshot_json="{}",
            status="failed_needs_reconciliation"
            if publication_state == "uncertain"
            else "succeeded",
            stage="reconcile" if publication_state == "uncertain" else "verify",
            finished_at=stale,
            created_at=stale,
            queued_at=stale,
            started_at=stale,
            reconciliation_required=publication_state == "uncertain",
            data_impact="uncertain" if publication_state == "uncertain" else "verified",
        )
        db.add(run)
        db.flush()
        run_id = run.id
        publication = DatabricksPublication(
            run_id=run.id,
            user_id=owner.id,
            workspace_id="a" * 64,
            connection_generation="test-generation",
            target_key="b" * 64,
            active_target_key="b" * 64 if publication_state == "uncertain" else None,
            target_locator_json=_table_locator().model_dump_json(),
            write_mode="databricks_append",
            staging_name="private.staging.audit",
            state=publication_state,
            submission_id=run.id,
            submitted_at=stale,
            created_at=stale,
            updated_at=stale,
            confirmed_at=stale if publication_state == "cleanup_pending" else None,
        )
        db.add(publication)
        db.commit()
        if publication_state == "uncertain":
            record_reconciliation_review(db, user=owner, run_id=run.id)
        assert db.get(DatabricksPublication, run_id) is not None
    with SessionLocal() as db:
        counts = janitor(db, settings)
        assert counts["runs"] == 1
        assert db.get(DatabricksPublication, run_id) is None
    print(
        f"Janitor cascaded unresolved {publication_state} publication, including its fence/evidence"
    )
```

</details>

## Expected Behavior

Retain unresolved publication evidence and any active target fence until provider reconciliation and required cleanup finish, regardless of the ordinary run-retention cutoff or a recorded operator review.

## Actual Behavior

Both runs are purged and their publication rows disappear through ON DELETE CASCADE. The uncertain case loses its active target fence; the confirmed-commit case loses the only durable record directing staging cleanup. Both cases pass executable characterization assertions.

## Root Cause Analysis

janitor checks only run-level reconciliation requirements/review flags before deletion. It never checks DatabricksPublication.state, active_target_key, or pending cleanup. The foreign key cascades deletion to the durable operation table, bypassing its recovery lifecycle and uniqueness fence.

## Impact

A long-unresolved publication can lose its recovery/audit evidence and the database constraint that prevents another publication to the same target. Confirmed publications can leave remote staging data indefinitely. Defaults allow this after 90 days; supported shorter retention settings shorten the window. Loss of the fence is verified in persistence; no live duplicate Databricks write was attempted.

## Suggested Fix

Protect runs and their events whenever an associated publication is unresolved, owns a fence, or still needs staging cleanup. Resolve the provider operation before allowing run deletion, or retain publication evidence independently with suitable referential integrity. Operator review must not substitute for provider commit/cleanup confirmation.

## Test Coverage Gaps

The existing janitor test protects an unreviewed uncertain run but does not attach a DatabricksPublication. Recovery tests cover operation states independently of run retention. Add both reproduced cases, an unreviewed control, and resolved complete/unchanged publication controls.

## Severity

High

## Confidence

High — reproduced locally through the code paths and boundaries identified above.

## Existing Issue Matches

Reviewed all open issues (0 at audit start), 100 recently updated closed issues, the prior audit, and the complete patches of open documentation PRs #151 and #153. Each finding also received function/error/symptom searches across all issue states and open PRs. README, provider notes, the worker runbook, and relevant security decisions were checked for expected limitations.

Searched janitor, retention, DatabricksPublication, cascade, fence, and cleanup. #158 concerns a committed record excluded from the recovery selector; that selector now includes committed, but this report concerns deletion of the record itself by a different service. No existing report or open PR covers the retention/cascade defect.

new.title: [BUG] Databricks conflates TIMESTAMP_NTZ with TIMESTAMP and misses semantic schema changes
new.description: Databricks inspection erases the distinction between TIMESTAMP_NTZ and TIMESTAMP. Their normalized schemas and schema fingerprints are identical, and copying an NTZ source into a new Delta destination generates a TIMESTAMP staging column. Append compatibility uses the same conflated mapping.
new.steps:
1. Inspect a Unity Catalog Delta table whose column is reported as TIMESTAMP_NTZ.
2. Have the same object report TIMESTAMP for that column and inspect it again.
3. Compare the schemas and schema fingerprints.
4. Prepare a new Databricks target from the original NTZ schema and inspect the real adapter's generated CREATE TABLE SQL.
new.expected: Preserve wall-clock/no-zone and instant/session-zone semantics as distinct types through inspection, fingerprinting, append checks, extraction, and destination creation; alternatively reject an unsupported type explicitly before a transfer.
new.actual: Both schemas are `Datetime(time_unit='us')` and have identical fingerprints. The NTZ copy emits a staging declaration containing `occurred TIMESTAMP`, with no TIMESTAMP_NTZ. This is verified using the real adapter and the repository's controlled SQL/management harness; a live workspace was not contacted.
new.cause: Both native SQL type names map to the same Polars label in _SQL_TYPES. inspect_object fingerprints that normalized label instead of retaining the native semantic type, and _sql_type maps the resulting label only to TIMESTAMP. The lost distinction cannot be recovered by the writer.
new.impact: Wall-clock data can become an instant-based type without an explicit conversion, and a source or target TIMESTAMP/NTZ change can evade schema-drift checks. The generated type and fingerprint collision are confirmed; the exact value shift for a particular live SQL session depends on provider/session timezone behavior and is not claimed as a live acceptance result. Databricks documents the distinction in its [TIMESTAMP_NTZ reference](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/data-types/timestamp-ntz-type) and [TIMESTAMP reference](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/data-types/timestamp-type).
new.fix: Carry native temporal semantics in the connector schema, preserve them in schema fingerprints, and map naive NTZ and instant timestamps to the appropriate Delta and Polars types. Recheck append compatibility using those distinctions. Reject variants the connector cannot preserve.
new.gaps: Timestamp mapping tests cover the presence of a supported timestamp but not the difference between the two native families. Add distinct fingerprints and writer declarations, negative append/drift cases, and live round-trip acceptance with non-UTC sessions.
new.dedup: Exact all-state TIMESTAMP_NTZ searches returned no issues. Also reviewed #27 (PostgreSQL timestamptz semantics), #155 (false drift from Polars string spelling), and #156 (Databricks rejecting parameterized dtype spelling). This is distinct: accepted native Databricks temporal families collapse to the same type and fingerprint. No open fix found.

Databricks inspection erases the distinction between TIMESTAMP_NTZ and TIMESTAMP. Their normalized schemas and schema fingerprints are identical, and copying an NTZ source into a new Delta destination generates a TIMESTAMP staging column. Append compatibility uses the same conflated mapping.

Verified October 27, 2026 on commit `2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0`. Baseline: **990 passed**. Audit: **14 passing characterization cases across 8 distinct defects** (including three existing-report matches). Python 3.12.13, Polars 1.44.2, psycopg 3.3.5. No production data or live provider credentials were used.

## Labels

`bug`, `priority: high`.

## Affected Components

- [_SQL_TYPES](https://github.com/eddiethedean/user-token-management-app/blob/2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0/app/connectors/databricks.py#L67)
- [DatabricksConnector.inspect_object and schema fingerprint](https://github.com/eddiethedean/user-token-management-app/blob/2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0/app/connectors/databricks.py#L361)
- [_polars_type](https://github.com/eddiethedean/user-token-management-app/blob/2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0/app/connectors/databricks.py#L1338)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Inspect a Unity Catalog Delta table whose column is reported as TIMESTAMP_NTZ.
2. Have the same object report TIMESTAMP for that column and inspect it again.
3. Compare the schemas and schema fingerprints.
4. Prepare a new Databricks target from the original NTZ schema and inspect the real adapter's generated CREATE TABLE SQL.

Save the following self-contained test outside `tests/`, for example `/tmp/test_bug.py`. Install the repository's development dependencies, then run from the repository root:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest /tmp/test_bug.py -c pyproject.toml -s --tb=short
```

PostgreSQL cases require the local server binaries used by the repository fixtures. All databases and HTTP services are disposable loopback fixtures. Databricks cases use the existing SQL/management harness. **These are characterization assertions: passing means the defect was reproduced.** Invert them when adding regression tests.

<details>
<summary>Executable reproduction</summary>

```python
from __future__ import annotations
import uuid
from app.connectors.locators import DatabricksCreatePolicy
from tests.test_databricks_connector import _sql_connector, _SQLHarness, _table_locator

pytest_plugins = ["tests.conftest"]


def test_databricks_loses_timestamp_ntz_identity(access_app):
    harness = _SQLHarness(
        exists=True, columns=[("occurred", "timestamp_ntz", "TIMESTAMP_NTZ", "YES")]
    )
    source, credentials = _sql_connector(harness)
    schema_ntz = source.inspect_object(credentials, _table_locator())
    harness.columns = [("occurred", "timestamp", "TIMESTAMP", "YES")]
    schema_tz = source.inspect_object(credentials, _table_locator())
    assert schema_ntz.columns == schema_tz.columns
    assert schema_ntz.schema_fingerprint == schema_tz.schema_fingerprint

    target_harness = _SQLHarness(exists=False)
    destination, credentials = _sql_connector(target_harness)
    credentials["_publication_event"] = lambda *a, **kw: None
    load = destination.prepare_destination(
        credentials,
        _table_locator(table="copy_of_ntz"),
        schema_ntz,
        DatabricksCreatePolicy(),
        run_id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
    )
    create = next(sql for sql, _ in target_harness.statements if sql.startswith("CREATE TABLE"))
    assert "`occurred` TIMESTAMP" in create
    assert "TIMESTAMP_NTZ" not in create
    destination.abort(load)
    print(
        "TIMESTAMP and TIMESTAMP_NTZ have identical schema fingerprints; NTZ copy declares TIMESTAMP"
    )
```

</details>

## Expected Behavior

Preserve wall-clock/no-zone and instant/session-zone semantics as distinct types through inspection, fingerprinting, append checks, extraction, and destination creation; alternatively reject an unsupported type explicitly before a transfer.

## Actual Behavior

Both schemas are `Datetime(time_unit='us')` and have identical fingerprints. The NTZ copy emits a staging declaration containing `occurred TIMESTAMP`, with no TIMESTAMP_NTZ. This is verified using the real adapter and the repository's controlled SQL/management harness; a live workspace was not contacted.

## Root Cause Analysis

Both native SQL type names map to the same Polars label in _SQL_TYPES. inspect_object fingerprints that normalized label instead of retaining the native semantic type, and _sql_type maps the resulting label only to TIMESTAMP. The lost distinction cannot be recovered by the writer.

## Impact

Wall-clock data can become an instant-based type without an explicit conversion, and a source or target TIMESTAMP/NTZ change can evade schema-drift checks. The generated type and fingerprint collision are confirmed; the exact value shift for a particular live SQL session depends on provider/session timezone behavior and is not claimed as a live acceptance result. Databricks documents the distinction in its [TIMESTAMP_NTZ reference](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/data-types/timestamp-ntz-type) and [TIMESTAMP reference](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/sql/language-manual/data-types/timestamp-type).

## Suggested Fix

Carry native temporal semantics in the connector schema, preserve them in schema fingerprints, and map naive NTZ and instant timestamps to the appropriate Delta and Polars types. Recheck append compatibility using those distinctions. Reject variants the connector cannot preserve.

## Test Coverage Gaps

Timestamp mapping tests cover the presence of a supported timestamp but not the difference between the two native families. Add distinct fingerprints and writer declarations, negative append/drift cases, and live round-trip acceptance with non-UTC sessions.

## Severity

High

## Confidence

High — reproduced locally through the code paths and boundaries identified above.

## Existing Issue Matches

Reviewed all open issues (0 at audit start), 100 recently updated closed issues, the prior audit, and the complete patches of open documentation PRs #151 and #153. Each finding also received function/error/symptom searches across all issue states and open PRs. README, provider notes, the worker runbook, and relevant security decisions were checked for expected limitations.

Exact all-state TIMESTAMP_NTZ searches returned no issues. Also reviewed #27 (PostgreSQL timestamptz semantics), #155 (false drift from Polars string spelling), and #156 (Databricks rejecting parameterized dtype spelling). This is distinct: accepted native Databricks temporal families collapse to the same type and fingerprint. No open fix found.

## Description

A saved Decimal override on a PostgreSQL text source succeeds or fails solely according to batch boundaries. Rows `1.2` and `1.23` succeed in one batch, but fail at Foundry finalization when split into two batches. Both values fit losslessly in a common Decimal.

Verified October 27, 2026 on commit `2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0`. Baseline: **990 passed**. Audit: **14 passing characterization cases across 8 distinct defects** (including three existing-report matches). Python 3.12.13, Polars 1.44.2, psycopg 3.3.5. No production data or live provider credentials were used.

## Labels

`bug`, `priority: medium`.

## Affected Components

- [_decimal_dtype](https://github.com/eddiethedean/user-token-management-app/blob/2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0/app/services/column_casting.py#L136)
- [cast_batch_columns](https://github.com/eddiethedean/user-token-management-app/blob/2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0/app/services/column_casting.py#L68)
- [_lossless_common_dtype](https://github.com/eddiethedean/user-token-management-app/blob/2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0/app/connectors/foundry.py#L79)
- [_lossless_common_schema](https://github.com/eddiethedean/user-token-management-app/blob/2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0/app/connectors/foundry.py#L114)
- [FoundryConnector.finalize](https://github.com/eddiethedean/user-token-management-app/blob/2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0/app/connectors/foundry.py#L1329)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a PostgreSQL source with text values `1.2` and `1.23`.
2. Save a PostgreSQL-to-MSS/MCS-COP route with the amount column cast to Decimal.
3. Execute with PIPELINE_BATCH_ROWS=1.
4. Execute the same route/data with PIPELINE_BATCH_ROWS=2.

Save the following self-contained test outside `tests/`, for example `/tmp/test_bug.py`. Install the repository's development dependencies, then run from the repository root:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest /tmp/test_bug.py -c pyproject.toml -s --tb=short
```

PostgreSQL cases require the local server binaries used by the repository fixtures. All databases and HTTP services are disposable loopback fixtures. Databricks cases use the existing SQL/management harness. **These are characterization assertions: passing means the defect was reproduced.** Invert them when adding regression tests.

<details>
<summary>Executable reproduction</summary>

```python
from __future__ import annotations
import io
from decimal import Decimal
import polars as pl
import pytest
from app.config import get_settings
from app.connectors.errors import ConnectorError, TransferErrorCode
from app.connectors.locators import DefinitionSnapshot, FoundryReplaceFilePolicy, FoundryUploadLocator, postgres_table
from app.connectors.mss import MssConnector
from app.connectors.postgres import PostgresConnector, connect
from app.database import SessionLocal
from app.models import PipelineRun
from app.services.pipeline_runs import claim_run
from app.services.transfer_engine import execute_transfer
from tests.postgres_support import connector_settings

pytest_plugins = ["tests.conftest"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("batch_rows", [1, 2])
def test_foundry_decimal_override_depends_on_batch_size(
    access_app, make_user, postgres_credentials, tmp_path, batch_rows
):
    from tests.simulators.foundry import FOUNDRY_DATASET, FOUNDRY_TOKEN, FoundrySimulator

    owner = make_user("decimal.audit@example.gov")
    cfg = connector_settings()
    with connect(postgres_credentials, cfg) as conn:
        conn.execute("CREATE TABLE audit_source (amount text)")
        conn.execute("INSERT INTO audit_source VALUES ('1.2'), ('1.23')")
    simulator = FoundrySimulator()
    settings = get_settings().model_copy(
        update={"pipeline_spool_root": str(tmp_path), "pipeline_batch_rows": batch_rows}
    )
    target = FoundryUploadLocator(
        dataset_rid=FOUNDRY_DATASET, branch="master", file_name="copy.parquet"
    )
    snapshot = DefinitionSnapshot(
        name="Decimal override audit",
        source_provider="postgres",
        destination_provider="mss",
        source=postgres_table("public", "audit_source"),
        destination=target,
        write_policy=FoundryReplaceFilePolicy(column_type_overrides={"amount": "decimal"}),
    )
    with simulator.serve(), SessionLocal() as db:
        run = PipelineRun(user_id=owner.id, definition_snapshot_json=snapshot.model_dump_json())
        db.add(run)
        db.commit()
        run, lease = claim_run(db, worker_id="audit", lease_seconds=120, run_id=run.id)

        def execute():
            execute_transfer(
                db,
                run=run,
                lease_token=lease,
                snapshot=snapshot,
                source_credentials=postgres_credentials,
                destination_credentials={
                    "endpoint": simulator.base_url,
                    "token": FOUNDRY_TOKEN,
                    "dataset_rid": FOUNDRY_DATASET,
                },
                settings=settings,
                cancel_requested=lambda: False,
                source_resolver=lambda _: PostgresConnector(cfg),
                destination_resolver=lambda _: MssConnector(settings),
                route_policy=lambda *_: True,
                writer_policy=lambda _: True,
            )

        if batch_rows == 1:
            with pytest.raises(ConnectorError) as failure:
                execute()
            assert failure.value.code == TransferErrorCode.SCHEMA_DRIFT
            assert "incompatible column types" in failure.value.summary
            assert "copy.parquet" not in simulator.files
            print("Decimal override failed for 1.2 / 1.23 split across batches; no upload")
        else:
            execute()
            assert run.status == "succeeded"
            frame = pl.read_parquet(io.BytesIO(simulator.files["copy.parquet"]))
            assert frame["amount"].to_list() == [Decimal("1.20"), Decimal("1.23")]
            print("Identical Decimal override and data succeeded when both rows share a batch")
```

</details>

## Expected Behavior

Both runs succeed with exact Decimal values 1.20 and 1.23. Changing the supported batch size must not change whether a valid column can transfer.

## Actual Behavior

One-row batches raise SCHEMA_DRIFT: Foundry batches have incompatible column types; no file was published. Two rows in one batch succeed and the uploaded Parquet contains Decimal 1.20 and 1.23. The reproduction uses the real transfer engine and PostgreSQL connector with the local Foundry HTTP simulator.

## Root Cause Analysis

_decimal_dtype chooses scale separately for each batch, producing Decimal(38,1) and Decimal(38,2). _lossless_common_dtype accepts identical types and selected integer/float promotions but has no safe Decimal scale reconciliation. Finalization therefore rejects data that a single-batch cast represents correctly.

## Impact

Valid production routes can fail late after completing source scanning and local staging, depending on row order, configured batch size, or byte-driven splitting. No remote file is published in the failing reproduction. PostgreSQL-to-Foundry routes with mixed fractional precision and a selected Decimal cast are affected.

## Suggested Fix

Determine a safe shared Decimal shape for the reviewed transfer, or reconcile observed decimal batches losslessly before publication. Preserve all required integer digits when increasing scale and reject only genuinely unrepresentable combinations beyond the supported precision.

## Test Coverage Gaps

Single-batch casts and fixed-schema decimal sources do not exercise per-batch scale inference. Add end-to-end Decimal overrides across varied batch sizes, null-only batches, differing fractional scales, and actual precision-overflow controls; assert exact uploaded Parquet values.

## Severity

Medium

## Confidence

High — reproduced locally through the code paths and boundaries identified above.

## Existing Issue Matches

Reviewed all open issues (0 at audit start), 100 recently updated closed issues, the prior audit, and the complete patches of open documentation PRs #151 and #153. Each finding also received function/error/symptom searches across all issue states and open PRs. README, provider notes, the worker runbook, and relevant security decisions were checked for expected limitations.

Searched _lossless_common_schema, column_type_overrides, incompatible column types, and Foundry/decimal/batch scales. #74 concerns silent integer-to-float promotion; #78 concerns the CSV parser losing decimal precision. This report starts from PostgreSQL text, selects an explicit Decimal cast, and fails before publication because generated decimal scales differ. No reasonable duplicate or open fix found.

```python
from app.connectors.foundry import FoundryConnector

pytest_plugins = ["tests.conftest"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("format", ["csv", "parquet"])
def test_empty_foundry_source_is_reported_missing(access_app, tmp_path, format):
    from tests.simulators.foundry import FOUNDRY_DATASET, FOUNDRY_TOKEN, FoundrySimulator

    simulator = FoundrySimulator()
    path = "notes.csv" if format == "csv" else "readiness.parquet"
    if format == "csv":
        simulator.files[path] = b"value,label\n"
    else:
        buffer = io.BytesIO()
        pl.DataFrame(schema={"value": pl.Int64, "label": pl.String}).write_parquet(buffer)
        simulator.files[path] = buffer.getvalue()
    settings = get_settings().model_copy(update={"pipeline_spool_root": str(tmp_path)})
    with simulator.serve():
        connector = FoundryConnector(settings)
        credentials = {
            "endpoint": simulator.base_url,
            "token": FOUNDRY_TOKEN,
            "dataset_rid": FOUNDRY_DATASET,
        }
        source = FoundryDatasetFilesLocator(
            dataset_rid=FOUNDRY_DATASET, branch="master", file_paths=[path]
        )
        schema = connector.inspect_object(credentials, source)
        assert [column.name for column in schema.columns] == ["value", "label"]
        with pytest.raises(ConnectorError) as failure:
            list(connector.extract(credentials, source, batch_rows=10, batch_bytes=10000))
        assert failure.value.code == TransferErrorCode.SOURCE_NOT_FOUND
        assert "no CSV or Parquet files" in failure.value.summary
    print(
        f"Existing zero-row Foundry {format} is inspected successfully, then reported as no files"
    )
```

```python
def _execute_postgres(db, owner, credentials, *, settings=None):
    snapshot = DefinitionSnapshot(
        name="PostgreSQL type audit",
        source_provider="postgres",
        destination_provider="postgres",
        source=postgres_table("public", "audit_source"),
        destination=postgres_table("public", "audit_target"),

        destination_resolver=lambda _: PostgresConnector(connector_settings()),
        route_policy=lambda *_: True,
        writer_policy=lambda _: True,
    )
    return run


def test_existing_timezone_issue_remains_on_current_head(
    access_app, make_user, postgres_credentials
):

    with connect(postgres_credentials, cfg) as conn:

        conn.execute("CREATE TABLE audit_target (value timestamp)")
        conn.execute("INSERT INTO audit_source VALUES ('2026-10-27 08:00:00-04')")

        run = _execute_postgres(db, owner, postgres_credentials)
        assert run.status == "succeeded"
        assert json.loads(run.verification_json)["verification_level"] == "exact"
    with connect(postgres_credentials, cfg) as conn:
        conn.execute("SET TIME ZONE 'America/New_York'")
        shift = conn.execute(
            "SELECT extract(epoch FROM (t.value::timestamptz - s.value)) "
            "FROM audit_source s CROSS JOIN audit_target t"
        ).fetchone()[0]
    assert shift == 14400
    print(
        "Existing #27: timezone semantics still lost; 14400-second difference after succeeded/exact"
    )
```

**Existing Issue Found:** #157 — CSV profiling accepts numeric and date syntax that extraction cannot parse. **Match confidence: High. Severity: Medium.**

- Uploaded CSV `T12:34:56` profiles as time, then raises UNSUPPORTED_TYPE during extraction.
- A quoted uploaded CSV value `12:34:56,123` also profiles as time, then fails extraction.
- A Foundry CSV value `2026-10-27 12:30` profiles as datetime; the lazy scan advertises that type, then collection raises InvalidOperationError. The upload connector accepts that same minute-only timestamp, confirming inconsistent execution grammars between adapters.

Affected current code: [_value_type](https://github.com/eddiethedean/user-token-management-app/blob/2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0/app/domain/csv_inference.py#L147), [_normalize_profiled_cells](https://github.com/eddiethedean/user-token-management-app/blob/2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0/app/connectors/csv_source.py#L232), and [_csv_file_scan](https://github.com/eddiethedean/user-token-management-app/blob/2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0/app/connectors/foundry.py#L848). The Foundry adapter normalizes additional time forms, while the upload path does not; Foundry's String-to-Datetime cast rejects some spellings the profiler accepts.

Expected/fix: every accepted typed profile must be executable. Share an explicit profiling/normalization/parsing contract, or classify unsupported forms as text before accepting the scan. Extend tests across both adapters for T-prefixed times, comma fractional seconds, minute-only timestamps, nulls, and mixed accepted formats. These are availability failures with no destination publication.

Verified October 27, 2026 on commit `2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0`. Baseline: **990 passed**. Audit: **14 passing characterization cases across 8 distinct defects** (including three existing-report matches). Python 3.12.13, Polars 1.44.2, psycopg 3.3.5. No production data or live provider credentials were used.

Save the following self-contained test outside `tests/`, for example `/tmp/test_bug.py`. Install the repository's development dependencies, then run from the repository root:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest /tmp/test_bug.py -c pyproject.toml -s --tb=short
```

PostgreSQL cases require the local server binaries used by the repository fixtures. All databases and HTTP services are disposable loopback fixtures. Databricks cases use the existing SQL/management harness. **These are characterization assertions: passing means the defect was reproduced.** Invert them when adding regression tests.

<summary>Executable reproduction</summary>

```python
from __future__ import annotations
import polars as pl
import pytest
from app.connectors.csv_source import CsvSourceConnector
from app.connectors.errors import ConnectorError, TransferErrorCode
from app.services.csv_uploads import inspect_csv
from tests.test_csv_decimal_precision import _csv_credentials, _locator

pytest_plugins = ["tests.conftest"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", ["T12:34:56", "12:34:56,123"])
def test_uploaded_csv_still_profiles_unparseable_time_values(value):
    content = ('value,label\n"' + value + '",ok\n').encode()
    inspection = inspect_csv("time.csv", content)
    assert inspection.columns[0].inferred_type == "time"
    credentials = _csv_credentials(content, inspection)
    credentials["quote_char"] = inspection.quote_char
    credentials["skip_initial_space"] = inspection.skip_initial_space
    with pytest.raises(ConnectorError) as failure:
        list(
            CsvSourceConnector().extract(credentials, _locator(), batch_rows=10, batch_bytes=10000)
        )
    assert failure.value.code == TransferErrorCode.UNSUPPORTED_TYPE
    print(f"Existing #157: CSV {value!r} profiles as time, then fails extraction")


def test_foundry_csv_still_profiles_unparseable_minute_timestamp(tmp_path):
    from app.connectors.foundry import _csv_file_scan

    path = tmp_path / "minutes.csv"
    path.write_bytes(b"occurred,label\n2026-10-27 12:30,ok\n")
    scan, profiles = _csv_file_scan(path)
    assert profiles[0].inferred_type == "datetime"
    with pytest.raises(pl.exceptions.InvalidOperationError):
        scan.collect()
    print(
        "Existing #157: Foundry CSV minute-only datetime profiles successfully, then fails extraction"
    )
```

</details>

An additional stale-health writer is still vulnerable on October 27, 2026 at `2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0`: `create_foundry_dataset`, even though `test_user_connection` now has revision/check-ID guards.

**Existing Issue Found:** #81 — Stale connection tests overwrite results for replacement credentials. **Match confidence: High. Severity: Medium.** Same user-visible defect and missing generation guard; adding the affected path here instead of opening a duplicate.

Deterministic reproduction: start dataset creation using saved credential bundle A; while its provider call is in flight, use a second real database session to replace A with B and persist a failed connection check for B; then let A's dataset creation succeed. The encrypted stored bundle remains B, but its validation_status becomes connected and its message claims authentication was established by successful dataset creation. The provider boundary is controlled and synthetic; encryption, persistence, replacement, health checking, and dataset service code are real.

Affected current code: [create_foundry_dataset](https://github.com/eddiethedean/user-token-management-app/blob/2dd38ef00ed3984663a0896e662989a97e7242e0/app/services/foundry_datasets.py#L40) (unconditional health assignment near its end). Unlike the protected tester, it does not predicate its health write on the credential revision used for the side effect. It also records the dataset created under A against the owner/provider slot now holding B.

Expected/fix: publish validation and dataset metadata only against the credential generation that performed the operation; treat the older completion as superseded. Preserve B's failed/untested health. Add deterministic interleavings for replacement and deletion during dataset creation. This produces false readiness and unusable selections; provider authorization is still enforced, and no authorization bypass is claimed.

<summary>Executable reproduction</summary>

```python
from __future__ import annotations
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import Mock
from app.config import get_settings
from app.connectors.base import ConnectionHealth, ProvisionedDataset
from app.database import SessionLocal
from app.models import User, UserSecret

pytest_plugins = ["tests.conftest"]


def test_dataset_creation_overwrites_replacement_connection_health(
    access_app, make_user, monkeypatch
):
    from sqlalchemy import select

    import app.services.foundry_datasets as datasets
    from app.services.secrets import (
        decrypt_user_credentials_for_run,
        store_user_credentials,
        test_user_connection,
    )

    owner = make_user("dataset.race.audit@example.gov")
    settings = get_settings()
    old = {"endpoint": "https://old.demo.invalid", "token": "synthetic-old-token"}
    new = {"endpoint": "https://new.demo.invalid", "token": "synthetic-new-token"}
    with SessionLocal() as db:
        store_user_credentials(db, settings, user=owner, provider="mss", credentials=old)

    def interleaved_creation(credentials, *, parent_folder_rid, name):
        assert credentials["endpoint"] == old["endpoint"]
        with SessionLocal() as other:
            current_owner = other.get(User, owner.id)
            store_user_credentials(
                other, settings, user=current_owner, provider="mss", credentials=new
            )
            failed = Mock()
            failed.test_connection.return_value = ConnectionHealth(
                status="failed", message="Replacement endpoint failed", latency_ms=1
            )
            checked = test_user_connection(
                other,
                user=current_owner,
                provider="mss",
                settings=settings,
                connector_resolver=lambda _: failed,
            )
            assert checked.validation_status == "failed"
        return ProvisionedDataset(
            dataset_rid="ri.foundry.main.dataset.synthetic-created",
            name=name,
            parent_folder_rid=parent_folder_rid,
        )

    provisioner = SimpleNamespace(
        capabilities=SimpleNamespace(dataset_creation=True), create_dataset=interleaved_creation
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(datasets, "dataset_provisioner_for", lambda _: provisioner)
    with SessionLocal() as db:
        datasets.create_foundry_dataset(
            db,
            settings,
            user=db.get(User, owner.id),
            provider="mss",
            parent_folder_rid="ri.compass.main.folder.synthetic",
            name="Audit dataset",
        )
    with SessionLocal() as db:
        stored = db.scalar(
            select(UserSecret).where(UserSecret.user_id == owner.id, UserSecret.provider == "mss")
        )
        current = decrypt_user_credentials_for_run(
            db, settings, user=db.get(User, owner.id), provider="mss"
        )
        assert current["endpoint"] == new["endpoint"]
        assert stored.validation_status == "connected"
        assert "successful dataset creation" in stored.validation_message
    print(
        "Existing #81: dataset creation on old credentials overwrote failed replacement health with connected"
    )
```
